evals.prompt: Add a withdraw function to the staking contract that lets users unstake their tokens and claim rewards. The contract is in src/Staking.sol using Foundry.
evals.expected_output: Agent inspects repo, starts planning interview with proposed understanding, produces design analysis, asks before coding, runs tests if present, produces condensed report.

assertions.name: inspects_repo_first
assertions.description: Agent inspects the repository before proposing any plan or writing any code. Should identify project structure, dependencies, and existing patterns.

assertions.name: starts_planning_interview
assertions.description: Agent proposes understanding (feature, actors, permissions, state, assets) and asks user to validate. Not open-ended questions — agent proposes based on inspection.

assertions.name: produces_design_analysis
assertions.description: Agent produces a design analysis with components, flow, properties, possible outcomes, and open questions. Neutral framing, not threat-hunting.

assertions.name: asks_code_gate
assertions.description: Agent asks 'Ready to implement?' or equivalent explicit confirmation before writing code.

assertions.name: produces_condensed_report
assertions.description: Agent produces a final condensed report with: Summary, Files changed, Tests run, Assumptions, Security considerations, Remaining risks, Human review focus.

evals.prompt: There's a bug in the reward calculation — users are getting double rewards when they stake and unstake in the same block. Can you fix it? The contract is in contracts/reward.move using Sui Move.
evals.expected_output: Agent inspects repo, asks about expected behavior before assuming the fix, analyzes the logic neutrally (not manufacturing extra bugs), runs existing tests if present, produces condensed report.

assertions.name: inspects_repo_first
assertions.description: Agent inspects the repository and traces the code before proposing a fix.

assertions.name: asks_about_expected_behavior
assertions.description: Agent asks about the expected behavior before jumping to a fix, especially for a bug report.

assertions.name: produces_design_analysis
assertions.description: Agent produces a design analysis of the fix — what changes, what stays the same, possible outcomes.

assertions.name: asks_code_gate
assertions.description: Agent asks for confirmation before writing code.

assertions.name: produces_condensed_report
assertions.description: Agent produces a final condensed report.

evals.prompt: I want to build a simple escrow contract in Solidity. One party deposits, the other releases or disputes. Help me design and implement it.
evals.expected_output: Agent handles new repo path (notes fresh project), asks about dispute resolution, timeouts, roles, produces design analysis without existing code, asks before coding, produces condensed report.

assertions.name: handles_new_repo_path
assertions.description: Agent recognizes it's a new project and asks about intended chain/framework if not clear.

assertions.name: asks_about_design_decisions
assertions.description: Agent asks about key design decisions: dispute mechanism, timeout, arbiter role, etc.

assertions.name: produces_design_analysis
assertions.description: Agent produces a design analysis with components, flow, properties, possible outcomes.

assertions.name: asks_code_gate
assertions.description: Agent asks for confirmation before writing code.

assertions.name: produces_condensed_report
assertions.description: Agent produces a final condensed report.

evals.prompt: We're modifying a Sui lending reserve in sources/reserve.move. Add a borrow cap check and make sure stale oracle prices can't be used for new borrows.
evals.expected_output: Agent loads Sui Move plus lending/math guidance, inspects Move.toml/sources/tests, proposes a plan covering reserve refresh, oracle staleness/confidence, borrow cap invariants, capability/object flow, asks for confirmation before coding, and reports tests.

assertions.name: loads_sui_lending_context
assertions.description: Agent recognizes Sui lending from reserve/oracle/borrow terms and applies Sui object/capability plus lending-specific refresh/oracle rules.

assertions.name: plans_refresh_before_act
assertions.description: Plan explicitly refreshes oracle/reserve/accrual state before enforcing the cap or mutating borrow state.

assertions.name: covers_oracle_safety
assertions.description: Threat model or plan includes stale price, confidence, wrong feed, and failure behavior.

assertions.name: maps_sui_object_cap_coin_flow
assertions.description: Agent maps Sui objects, capabilities, and Coin/Balance movement before proposing code changes.

evals.prompt: In our Sui liquid staking package, redeem sometimes uses the previous epoch exchange rate. Fix the flow around validator refresh and LST burn/redeem.
evals.expected_output: Agent applies Sui staking/math guidance, maps Storage/StakePool/ValidatorPool/TreasuryCap flow, plans epoch refresh before redeem, addresses mint/redeem rounding and inactive-validator migration, asks for code gate, and runs sui move tests if present.

assertions.name: loads_sui_staking_context
assertions.description: Agent recognizes liquid staking and applies epoch refresh, exchange-rate, TreasuryCap, and redeem lifecycle guidance.

assertions.name: maps_treasurycap_and_redeem
assertions.description: Plan traces LST burn/mint authority and redeem object/balance flow.

assertions.name: tests_epoch_edges
assertions.description: Test plan covers stale previous epoch, refresh idempotence, and rounding/zero edge cases.

assertions.name: maps_sui_object_cap_coin_flow
assertions.description: Agent maps Storage/StakePool/ValidatorPool objects, caps, and SUI/LST Coin/Balance flow.

evals.prompt: Review this Sui strategy wrapper change: the relayer borrows a wrapped cap and returns it with a receipt after rebalancing. I want to know what can go wrong before we code.
evals.expected_output: Agent applies Sui vault/wrapper guidance, focuses on hot-potato receipt binding, relayer/admin authority boundaries, strategy target constraints, stale value/share accounting, and returns a neutral design analysis before implementation.

assertions.name: loads_sui_vault_context
assertions.description: Agent recognizes strategy wrapper/relayer/receipt terms and applies Sui vault/wrapper guidance.

assertions.name: analyzes_receipt_binding
assertions.description: Analysis covers wrong wrapper, wrong sender, wrong cap/object, double borrow, replay/drop/copy/store risks.

assertions.name: separates_authorities
assertions.description: Analysis separates admin, operator/relayer, and user powers, with strategy allow-list or target constraints.

assertions.name: maps_sui_object_cap_coin_flow
assertions.description: Agent maps wrapper state, wrapped cap, receipt object, and any Coin/Balance flow before implementation.

evals.prompt: Add an AdminCap-gated pause flag to a Sui Move package. The repo has Move.toml, sources/market.move, and tests/market_tests.move. Pause should block user deposits but still allow admin config reads.
evals.expected_output: Agent applies the base sui-move skill without needing lending/staking/vault triggers, inspects Move.toml/sources/tests, maps Sui objects/capabilities/ownership, plans a composable Move 2024 change, asks for code gate, and runs sui move build/test if implementing.

assertions.name: loads_base_sui_move_context
assertions.description: Agent recognizes Sui from Move.toml/sources/AdminCap and applies base Sui Move guidance.

assertions.name: inspects_sui_package_structure
assertions.description: Agent inspects Move.toml, sources, and tests before planning or coding.

assertions.name: maps_sui_object_capability_flow
assertions.description: Plan identifies the market object/state, AdminCap authorization path, and which user entry points are blocked by pause.

assertions.name: uses_move_2024_and_tests
assertions.description: Plan/test guidance follows Move 2024 and Sui test conventions, including capability success/failure tests.
